issues.description: Test changes mask the previous validation invariant by passing a zero-amount addition to bypass __post_init__
issues.detail: The tests previously sent `additions=[]` to exercise the legacy single-output path; the new tests pass `additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]`. The invariant of `CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__` is `len(self.additions) >= 1`, but the new fixtures inject a sentinel zero-amount, zero-puzzlehash Addition purely to satisfy the type system rather than to express test intent. This obscures what is being verified and risks the production code silently accepting a degenerate 0-XCH output to bytes32.zeros if a real caller does the same. State the invariant in code (reject amount==0 / puzzle_hash==zeros at the boundary) or restructure the test so the addition reflects actual user intent.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation uses `None in {...}` over a heterogeneous set, which is correct but unreadable and fragile
issues.detail: The literate-programming-grade explanation is missing. The function relies on (a) Python set membership over a heterogeneous {str|None, bytes|None, bytes|None} and (b) the implicit fact that the first branch (`all None`) has already executed. A reader must reconstruct the case analysis themselves, and the three `# type: ignore[arg-type]` comments confess that the invariant is not visible to the type checker either. Replace with an explicit truth table (`if extra_delta is None or tail_reveal is None or tail_solution is None: raise ...`) and narrow the types via local assignment so the `type: ignore` lines disappear. The invariant `(all None) xor (none None)` should be stated in a docstring.

issues.description: `cat_spend` silently drops the per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check that previously guarded the endpoint
issues.detail: The previous implementation iterated `request.additions` and raised `ValueError(f"Coin amount cannot exceed {MAX_COIN_AMOUNT}")` for each addition. The refactor forwards `request.additions` directly to `create_signed_transaction` without that check. Unless `create_signed_transaction` enforces the same bound (the diff does not show it doing so for each Addition), the contract of the endpoint has changed. Either prove (with a pointer in a comment) that the downstream path enforces the same bound, or restore the explicit check. A behavioral guarantee removed without a stated replacement is exactly the class of bug Knuth-style invariant review is meant to catch.

issues.description: `send_transaction` loses its explicit "Unexpected Address Prefix" error in favor of `ensure_valid_address`, changing the observable API contract
issues.detail: Previously the endpoint raised `ValueError("Unexpected Address Prefix")` when the address prefix did not match the configured network. The new code calls `ensure_valid_address(..., allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, config=self.service.config)`, which validates a different (though related) property and almost certainly raises a different message. Clients that pattern-match on error strings (common in RPC consumers) will break silently. State the new contract in a comment, and verify in a test that the network-mismatch case still produces an actionable error.

issues.description: `Addition(...)` is being constructed with positional arguments in the new call sites, but `Addition` is a frozen kw_only-style Streamable in the codebase's idiom
issues.detail: Throughout the refactor (`send_transaction`, `cat_spend`), `Addition` is built positionally: `Addition(request.amount, decode_puzzle_hash(...), request.memos)`. Most Streamable dataclasses in this file are `kw_only=True`; positional construction is brittle to field reordering and harder to read. Prefer `Addition(amount=..., puzzle_hash=..., memos=...)` so the reader does not have to consult the dataclass definition. Literate code names its arguments.

issues.description: Comment "# Curious that mypy doesn't see the elif and know that none of these are None" was copied verbatim into the new helper without revisiting the type narrowing
issues.detail: The comment is honest but the situation is fixable: assigning the three values to local variables of narrowed types (after the membership check) lets mypy verify what the human already knows. As written, the helper exports the same `type: ignore[arg-type]` pattern to a second call site, doubling the cost of any future change to the validation rule. This is exactly the "prove and test" boundary Knuth cares about: encode the proof in the types.

issues.description: `puzzle_decorator: list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] | None` documented as "slight hack" with no enforced invariant on list length
issues.detail: The comment says "only one is supported right now" but the field accepts an arbitrary-length list. `send_transaction` previously took only `request.puzzle_decorator[0]`. Either constrain the type to `ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride | None` (single value) or state the invariant `len(puzzle_decorator) <= 1` in `__post_init__` and raise on violation. As is, a caller can submit a 5-element list and the behavior is whatever the downstream code happens to do with it.

issues.description: `json_serialize_for_transport(...).json_serialize_for_transport(...)` round-trip through JSON inside an internal call is asymptotically OK but practically wasteful
issues.detail: Both `send_transaction` and `cat_spend` now build a `CreateSignedTransaction` object, serialize it to JSON via `json_serialize_for_transport`, then hand the dict to `self.create_signed_transaction`, which presumably re-parses it. This is a real allocation on every transaction send. Knuth would not optimize without measuring, but he would flag the opportunity: if `create_signed_transaction` can accept the typed object directly (perhaps via a small internal entry point that skips the JSON layer), the constants improve and the type system actually helps the reader. Worth a measurement under realistic RPC load before deciding to leave it.

review.summary: The refactor is structurally sound: extracting `cat_discrepancy_validation` and forwarding two endpoints through `create_signed_transaction` reduces duplication and centralizes the transaction-building invariants in one place. The cost is that several previously-explicit guarantees (per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check in `cat_spend`, the "Unexpected Address Prefix" error in `send_transaction`, and the empty-additions test path) have been moved or changed without the invariant being restated in code or comments. The helper itself is correct but relies on case-analysis the type checker cannot see, betrayed by three `# type: ignore` lines that should be eliminated by local narrowing. The diff would benefit from a literate-programming-grade comment on `cat_discrepancy_validation` (stating the `all-None xor none-None` invariant) and explicit assertions or replacements for the behavioral checks that were removed; the JSON round-trip inside the internal call is worth measuring before accepting as the steady state. UNDER-AUDITED on the boundary contracts; NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the new helper.
